outputs.exact_statement:
There is a real radial Schwartz function $f:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ such that $$\label{intro:conditions}
  \widehat f(0)=1,\qquad f(0)=\frac{2}{\sqrt3},\qquad
  \widehat f(\xi)\ge0\quad(\xi\in\mathbb R^2),\qquad
  f(x)\le0\quad(|x|\ge1).$$

The function $q_p$ is real, radial, and Schwartz on $\mathbb R^2$, and $$\widehat{q_p}(\xi)=e^{-\pi hs}K_p(s),\qquad s=b\left\lvert\xi\right\rvert^2.$$ The function $K_p$ is entire and real on the real axis. Moreover, $$\label{fourier:damping}
 \operatorname{Im}z(t)
   =h\left(\frac{B}{t^2+h^2}-1\right)
   \ge\frac{26}{435}>0\qquad(-1\le t\le1).$$ Consequently every derivative of $K_p(s)$ decays exponentially as $s\to+\infty$.

For every specified triple $(i,m,y)$, put $$\label{signs:power-coefficients}
  T_r=\sigma_i y^r
       \frac{\widetilde H_i^{(r+\nu)}(m)}{(r+\nu)!},
  \qquad 0\le r\le28.$$ Then, for $0\le k\le28$, $$\label{signs:bernstein-bound}
  B_k:=\sum_{r=0}^k
       \frac{\binom{k}{r}}{\binom{28}{r}}T_r
  >\begin{cases}
      0.74,&m=0,\\
      0.18,&m=1,\\
      0.02,&m=3,4,\\
      0.009,&4<m\le40.
    \end{cases}$$
If $m\in12\mathbb Z+A$ is a nearest zero of $P$ to a real number $s$, then $$P(s)\ge0.68(s-m)^2.$$

The exact functions have the zero sets $$\label{signs:zero-sets}
 \{s\ge1:H_1(s)=0\}=\mathcal N,\qquad
 \{s\ge0:H_2(s)=0\}=\mathcal N,$$ and satisfy the strict inequalities $$H_1(s)<0\quad(s\ge1,\ s\notin\mathcal N),\qquad
 H_2(s)>0\quad(s\ge0,\ s\notin\mathcal N).$$ The zero of $H_1$ at $1$ is simple. Its zeros at $n\in\mathcal N$ with $n>1$, and the zeros of $H_2$ at every $n\in\mathcal N$, have order exactly two as zeros of the entire functions of $s$. Consequently $F(x)\le0$ when $b\left\lvert x\right\rvert^2\ge1$, and $\widehat F(\xi)\ge0$ for every $\xi\in\mathbb R^2$.

The Fourier pair constructed above satisfies $$\label{normalization:origin}
 F(0)=\widehat F(0)=6Q_1e^{-\pi h}>0.$$
If a periodic packing of disks of radius $1/2$ has covered-area density $\pi/(2\sqrt3)$, then its center set is the image of $\mathbb Z(1,0)+\mathbb Z(1/2,b)$ under a Euclidean isometry.

Let $p=PR$ have a real coefficient list supported in $\{0\}\cup I_f$, with $\|(c,d)\|_1\le3$, and let $C\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|C|\le1$. Let $m,y\in\mathbb R$ and $l\in\{0,\ldots,30\}$ satisfy $0\le m\le100$ and $|y|\le3/2$. The quadrature rule [cert:rule], with exact evaluations at its nodes and at the atoms, has error less than $10^{-22}$ in each moment $U_{p,l}(m,y)$ and $X_{p,l}(m,y)$.
For every $u\in\mathbb Q(i)$ satisfying $\Re(ip_*u)\le0$ and $|p_*u|\le1000$, the recursion [cert:estar] satisfies $$|e_*(u)-e^{ip_*u}|<3.542\cdot10^{-34}<10^{-32}.$$

Let $p=PR$ have a rational coefficient list supported in $\{0\}\cup I_f$, with $\|(c,d)\|_1\le3$, and let $C\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy $|C|\le1$. Let $m,y\in\mathbb Q$ and $l\in\{0,\ldots,30\}$ satisfy $0\le m\le100$ and $|y|\le3/2$. The prescription in Section 7.2 gives rational numbers $U_{p,l}^{\#}$ and $X_{p,l}^{\#}$ such that $$|U_{p,l}^{\#}-U_{p,l}|<10^{-14},\qquad |X_{p,l}^{\#}-X_{p,l}|<10^{-14}.$$ Separately, for every node $n\in12\mathbb Z+A$, using its residue $a\in A$ in [fourier:node-data], the prescribed rational values satisfy $$|Q_n^{\#}-Q_n|<10^{-25},\qquad |D_n^{\#}-D_n|<10^{-25}.$$

For each basis input $c_n=1$ or $d_n=1$, $n\in J$, with all other data zero, and each output node $m\in J$, the rational program computes both entries of $\mathcal S_m(p)$ with absolute error less than $10^{-12}$.

The following choices give sufficient rational error enclosures for the same finite quantities used in Appendix 6.* *For a basis input at $n\in J=\{1,3,4\}$, a row $m\in J$, $y=1$, and $\ell=0,1$, take $D=63$, $h_D=32$, $M=10^6$, and $\delta=10^{-14}$ in [ind:coefficient-budget]. There are no atoms. If $Q_m,D_m$ have rational errors at most $10^{-25}$, either entry of [cert:pair] has error less than $2.13\cdot10^{-13}<10^{-12}$.* *For the full rational finite-input domain at the start of this subsection, take $D=255$, $h_D=128$, $M=10^{53}$, and $\delta=4\cdot10^{-15}$ in [ind:coefficient-budget], and require each of the seven atom-product radii in [ind:atom-radii] to be at most $4\cdot10^{-15}/7$. Each $U$ and $X$ moment then has error less than $10^{-14}$. For node rows $m\in I_f$, with rational $Q_m,D_m$ errors at most $10^{-25}$, either entry of [cert:pair] has error less than $1.8\cdot10^{-14}$.
